intro: You already program, so you do not need to be told what a loop or a function is. This route skips the lessons that teach ideas you already know and keeps the ones that cover how Python does things differently: its truthiness rules, slicing, unpacking, comprehensions, argument passing, exceptions, classes, generators, decorators and tooling.

rows.expect: Variables are declared with a type and the type is fixed.
rows.python: A variable is just a name for a value. The type belongs to the value, so the same name can refer to different types over time.

rows.expect: Integers overflow, and / on integers divides as integers.
rows.python: int has no size limit, / is always true division, // floors (towards minus infinity) and % follows the sign of the divisor.
Any value can be a condition: 0, None, empty text and empty containers are falsy. and/or return one of their operands, not just True or False.

rows.expect: Strings are indexed one character at a time, and you build copies by hand.
rows.python: Strings are immutable sequences. Slices [start:stop:step] work on every sequence, and negative indexes count from the end.

rows.expect: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) with an index variable.
rows.python: for loops walk over items directly. Use enumerate when you need the position and zip to walk several sequences together.
rows.code:
for i, (letter, number) in enumerate(zip("ab", [10, 20])):
    print(i, letter, number)

rows.expect: Functions return one value, or you create a struct.
rows.python: Tuples group values, and unpacking takes them apart in one line, including swapping and collecting the rest with *.
rows.code:
first, (second, *rest) = 1, (2, 3, 4)
print(first, second, rest)
a, b = 1, 2
a, b = b, a
print(a, b)

rows.expect: Hash maps with a rigid API; sets from a library.
rows.python: dict and set are built in and have literals. dict.get gives defaults, dicts keep insertion order, and sets support | & - operators.

rows.expect: map and filter with lambdas, or loops that fill a list.
rows.python: A comprehension builds a list, dict or set in one readable expression. This is the idiomatic replacement for most small loops.
rows.code: print([n * n for n in range(6) if n % 2 == 0], {c: ord(c) for c in "ab"})

rows.python: One function takes defaults, keyword arguments, *args and **kwargs. Default values are created once, when the function is defined.

rows.expect: Pass by value or pass by reference.
rows.python: Arguments are names bound to the same objects. Mutating the object is visible to the caller, but rebinding the name is not.
rows.code:
def add(items):
    items.append(1)
    items = [99]

mine = []
add(mine)
print(mine)

rows.expect: Check first, then act (look before you leap).
rows.python: Python prefers to try the operation and handle the failure. try/except/else/finally is the full form; raise your own exceptions with built-in or custom classes.

rows.expect: try/finally or destructors to release resources.
rows.python: A with statement guarantees clean-up for files, locks and your own context managers.
rows.code:
from io import StringIO

with StringIO("a\nb") as f:
    print([line.strip() for line in f])
print(f.closed)

rows.expect: Declared fields, access modifiers, getters and setters.
rows.python: self is explicit, fields are created by assignment, and privacy is a naming convention (_name). Dunder methods such as __repr__ and __eq__ plug your class into the language.

rows.expect: Boilerplate constructors, equals and toString, plus getters and setters.
rows.python: @dataclass writes the boilerplate for you, and @property turns a method into a validated attribute without changing how callers use it.

rows.expect: Iterator classes, or collections built up front.
rows.python: yield turns a function into a lazy sequence. Generators can be endless and use almost no memory.
rows.code:
from itertools import islice

def evens():
    n = 0
    while True:
        yield n
        n += 2

print(list(islice(evens(), 4)))

rows.python: Functions are values, so a decorator is a function that takes a function and returns a new one. @name above a def applies it.

rows.expect: Static typing checked by the compiler.
rows.python: Type hints are optional documentation that tools such as mypy check. Python itself ignores them at runtime.

rows.expect: Build tools, XML project files and separate test frameworks.
rows.python: Each project gets a virtual environment (venv) and uses pip. Tests are plain functions with assert, run by pytest. A pyproject.toml describes how to build and install the project.
